tree.title: Tree
tree.description: A keyboard-accessible hierarchy for general nodes, department members, and files.
tree.playgroundNoSelection: Selection is disabled in display-only mode.
tree.playgroundActionHint: Use a row action or double-click a node to try onNodeAction.
tree.multiLevelActionsDescription: Deep branches keep their hierarchy clear with connector lines. renderActions reserves the row end for interactive controls such as a More menu without selecting or activating the row.
tree.actionHint: Open a node menu to try a row action.
tree.metricCatalogDescription: This production-scale example adapts domain JSON into Source → Resource → Category → Metric tree nodes. Semantic Hugeicons distinguish cloud sources, clusters, compute, network, storage, health, performance, categories, and metric leaves. Search matches labels, resource types, metric IDs, units, and dimensions; only metric leaves are selectable.
tree.metricCatalogDataNote: The source declares 236 metrics and names 224. ceph_osd declares 14 metrics but supplies only 2 names, so the JSON preserves the gap as “2 listed / 14” instead of inventing 12 metrics.
tree.metricCatalogSearchPlaceholder: Try CPU, device, percent, or k8s_node
tree.metricActionHint: Open a metric menu to try an action.
tree.selectionModesDescription: Use highlight mode for independent entity selection. Use checkbox cascade when a visible parent is an explicit switch for all eligible descendants.
tree.memberCascadeDescription: To select a department entity itself, use independent selection with
tree.entitySemanticsDescription: Choosing a department or folder returns that entity key. Member/file-only checkbox cascade returns eligible descendants and never inserts the collection parent key.
tree.selectedKeys: Selected keys: {keys}. The unresolved refresh key remains until the calling application clears it.
tree.constraintsDescription: Disabled branches are discoverable by keyboard but cannot expand or change selection. Read-only trees retain navigation and expansion while describing the constraint to assistive technology.
tree.statesTitle: Loading, error, empty, and no-result states
tree.accessibilityDescription: The tree uses one roving tab stop for its rows. Arrow keys move row focus without changing selection; Left and Right collapse, expand, or enter a branch; Home and End jump within visible rows; Space and Enter select or toggle a display-only branch; Ctrl/⌘+Enter invokes onNodeAction. Controls supplied through renderActions join the normal Tab order and keep their pointer and keyboard events separate from the row. Type a label prefix to move through visible rows. Checkbox cascade exposes true, false, and mixed values through aria-checked; highlight modes use aria-selected.
tree.accessibilityLimitation: Automated checks cover light and dark rendering, reduced motion, focus restoration, narrow layouts, long labels, and keyboard navigation. VoiceOver + Safari remains a release acceptance task in the consuming product because it depends on its surrounding landmarks and labels.
